facts.statement: Fluvionectes is a genus of elasmosaurid plesiosaur whose name means "river swimmer" in Latin and Greek.
facts.quote: Fluvionectes (meaning "river swimmer", from both Latin and Greek) is a genus of elasmosaurid plesiosaur found in the Dinosaur Park Formation in Alberta, Canada.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Fluvionectes was likely a young adult measuring between 5 and 5.2 meters long and weighing 392 kilograms.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen of Fluvionectes is a partial skeleton preserving an osteologically mature, likely a young adult individual that would have reached 5 - 5.2 m long and weighed 392 kg.

facts.statement: A larger, more mature specimen suggests that Fluvionectes may have reached a maximum body length of 7 meters.
facts.quote: A more mature, larger, but more fragmentary specimen (TMP 2009.037.0007) is also known, consisting of a partial rib and gastralium, and left humerus, indicating that this taxon may have reached 7 m in maximum body length.

facts.statement: The holotype skeleton contained 76 gastroliths, mostly disc-shaped stones made of black chert and grey quartzite, with the largest weighing 15.3 grams.
facts.quote: The holotype skeleton had 76 gastroliths, largely disc-shaped stones. All were composed of black chert and grey quartzite, the largest of which weighed 15.3 grams.

facts.statement: Fluvionectes is classified in the family Elasmosauridae and the subfamily Elasmosaurinae, sharing a clade with Albertonectes, Nakonanectes, Styxosaurus, and Terminonatator.
facts.quote: The describers placed Fluvionectes in Elasmosauridae, in a clade with Albertonectes, Nakonanectes, Styxosaurus, and Terminonatator, which by definition places it in the Elasmosaurinae subfamily.

facts.statement: Fluvionectes appears to have lived in freshwater and brackish water environments, unlike most other elasmosaurs which were oceanic.
facts.quote: Fluvionectes appears to have been a freshwater and brackish water animal based on its discovery from a non-marine to paralic sedimentary unit.

facts.statement: Evidence suggests Fluvionectes may have died after being caught in a log jam, as the holotype was found with coalified wood.
facts.quote: The holotype was discovered alongside many pieces of coalified wood, which is interpreted as the carcass having been caught in a log jam.

facts.statement: Fluvionectes lived during the Campanian stage, between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Fluvionectes is known from a single holotype specimen that includes parts of the trunk region.
facts.quote: Se conoce a partir de un único ejemplar, el holotipo, que incluye partes de la zona del tronco.
